newsitem.title: SPAIN: Mannesmann, AT&T in talks over Spain's Retevision.
newsitem.headline: Mannesmann, AT&T in talks over Spain's Retevision.

text.p: German mobile phone operator Mannesmann AG is in talks with U.S-based AT&T Corp over joining its bid for 60 percent of Spain's Retevision, the Spanish broadcaster said on Monday.
Retevision said the Unisource telecoms group had also formally indicated it was interested in bidding for what will become Spain's second telephone operator.
"Mannesmann has informed us that it is in talks with AT&T in order to incorporate it into (Mannesmann's) consortium," Retevision said in a statement.
"Furthermore, the Unisource group sent a formal declaration in order to participate in the auction."
The AT&T-led Unisource is a consortium of telecoms flagships from the Netherlands, Switzerland and Sweden.

Retevision added that the bid managers were studying Unisource's written request to see if it could be accepted as a valid expression of interest. The deadline for groups interested in bidding for the 60 percent stake was Monday.

Retevision said three international consortia had presented petitions to join the bid: Mannesmann; a group including Deutsche Telekom, France Telecom, Sprint Corp and BCH ; and a group including STET International, Endesa, Union Fenosa, Basque group Euskatel and various Basque banks.
Retevision chairman Pedro de Torres welcomed the participation of the main European operators, two U.S. operators and important Spanish companies in the bid.

"The project of creating through Retevision a global operator in telecommunications in Spain is attractive for investors and a good way to introduce competition in the telephone market," he said in a statement from the company.
